rule: As in haiku-both: of the aims meeting the criterion, the one named by the most citizens; a tie broken by the number of day-1 entries, posts and proposals naming it. Spreading bank shifts so the bank's balance lasts: 10 citizens, 87 entries (it became rule P1, passed 7–0 at cycle 20). The house count of cycles 1–4: 8 citizens, 21 entries. The notice's wording is the citizens' own: «spreading bank shifts» (Dune's press post no. 1, cycle 14; Heath and others).
reading: One post and one proposal in day 1. Citizens worked (Dune and Heath at the bank from c3), watched the bank fall from 1000 (Fern and Juniper logged it each cycle from c6), and at c14 Dune posted the ledger with «Heath proposes spreading bank shifts so the bank's share is left for others». From then the aim spread to all ten; North House (Cedar, Gale, Iris, Elm) held its votes until «Heath's wording» was in the hall; Birch filed it as P1 at c20 (spread bank shifts to the market, workshop and press; check the ledger once a day) and it passed 7–0 the same cycle. Heath's own text was never filed; North House was still waiting for it at c24.
